The '''2008–09 [[La Liga]]''' season (known as the ''Liga BBVA'' for sponsorship reasons) was the 78th since its establishment. [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] were the defending champions, having won their 31st La Liga title in [[2007–08 La Liga|the previous season]]. The campaign began on 30 August 2008, and concluded on 31 May 2009. A total of 20 teams contested the league, 17 of which already contested in the 2007–08 season, and three of which were promoted from the [[Segunda División]]. A new match ball – the [[Nike Inc.|Nike]] T90 Omni – served as the official ball for all matches.

On 16 May 2009, following [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]]'s 3–2 victory over Real Madrid, [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] were declared champions, winning their 19th La Liga title, with three matches to play. Barcelona's [[Lionel Messi]] received the inaugural [[La Liga Awards|La Liga Award for Best Player]] from the [[Liga Nacional de Fútbol Profesional]].

==Promotion and relegation==
[[Real Zaragoza]], [[Real Murcia]] and [[Levante UD|Levante]] were relegated to the [[2008–09 Segunda División]] after finishing in the bottom three spots of the table at the end of the 2007–08 La Liga. Zaragoza were relegated to the Segunda División after five seasons of continuous membership in the top football league of Spain; Levante returned in Segunda División after two-year tenured in La Liga; and Murcia made their immediate return to the second level.

The three relegated teams were replaced by three [[2007–08 Segunda División]] sides. Champions [[CD Numancia|Numancia]], who ended their second-level status after three years, runners-up [[Málaga CF|Málaga]], who returned to the top flight after two season in the second level, and [[Sporting de Gijón]] returned to the highest Spanish league after ten years.

Instead, following the signing of a five-year agreement with the humanitarian organisation UNICEF in 2006,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-09-13 |title=Barça take the moral high road |url=http://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/sep/13/barcelona |access-date=2022-11-29 |website=the Guardian |language=en}}</ref> the club sported the UNICEF logo on the front of its jersey while making an annual donation to the organisation.

==Awards==

===La Liga Awards===

===Zamora Trophy===
The [[Ricardo Zamora Trophy]] is awarded by newspaper ''[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]'' to the goalkeeper with the lowest ratio of goals conceded to matches played. A goalkeeper had to play at least 28 matches of 60 or more minutes to be eligible for the trophy.
